title: Autoscaler: add forecast ingestion interface + confidence gating scaffolding (no behavior change by default)
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Context
ENG-2844 is the MVP “predictive signal service” workstream. This PR is intentionally limited to plumbing + scaffolding in the fleet autoscaler so we can ingest forecasts (when available) and gate their influence on scaling decisions based on confidence. By design, this PR does NOT change current scaling behavior unless an internal flag is enabled.

What’s in this PR
- Introduce a ForecastProvider interface + request/response types for per-pool short-horizon demand forecasts.
- Add a forecast ingestion step to the scaling decision pipeline (wired, but backed by a stub provider returning “unavailable”).
- Implement confidence gating scaffolding:
  - If forecast is missing OR confidence < threshold => ignore forecast and fall back to reactive-only desired.
  - If confidence >= threshold => compute a “forecast_desired” candidate (still not used for actuation in this PR; we only emit it + gating decision for observability).
- Add structured decision annotations to the existing decision log payload (kept behind existing cardinality guardrails):
  - forecast_status: unavailable|stale|ok
  - forecast_confidence: float (bucketed)
  - forecast_horizon_s
  - forecast_desired_replicas
  - forecast_gate_reason: disabled|unavailable|low_confidence|ok
- Add config knobs (policy-evaluated defaults) but keep them inert:
  - predictive_scaling.enabled (default false)
  - predictive_scaling.min_confidence (default 0.8)
  - predictive_scaling.max_forecast_age_s (default 120)

Important: behavior safety
- Default behavior is unchanged. The stub provider returns forecast_status=unavailable, gate_reason=unavailable, and the autoscaler uses the existing reactive desired.
- No changes to bounds enforcement; the clamp logic remains the last step.

Implementation notes
- The ForecastProvider is injected via the autoscaler controller wiring to avoid hidden globals. The concrete provider implementation will land in the predictive-signal-service PRs; this PR only includes a NullForecastProvider.
- Confidence bucketing is done locally (0.0–0.2, 0.2–0.4, …, 0.8–1.0) to avoid high-cardinality metrics/events.
- Staleness check uses controller time to avoid clock skew in the provider implementation.

Illustrative snippet
interface ForecastProvider {
  getPoolForecast(ctx, { pool_id, region, now }): {
    status: 'ok'|'unavailable'|'error',
    generated_at_ms?: number,
    horizon_s?: number,
    predicted_qps?: number,
    predicted_token_rate?: number,
    confidence?: number
  }
}

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - gating logic: unavailable, stale, low confidence, ok
  - confidence bucketing boundaries
  - “no behavior change” assertion: desired_replicas unchanged when predictive_scaling.enabled=false
- Integration-ish test: controller wiring uses NullForecastProvider by default; decision log contains forecast fields.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Actual provider implementation that calls the predictive signal service (ENG-2844)
- Blending logic that turns forecast candidate into actuation (ENG-2845)
- Dashboards/alerts for forecast gating outcomes (ENG-2846)

Refs
- ADR-0143 Predictive signal blending (confidence gating, fallbacks)
- ENG-2843 Hard bounds enforcement (still authoritative)
commits: autoscaler: add ForecastProvider interface and NullForecastProvider
autoscaler: compute forecast candidate + confidence gating decision (inert by default)
autoscaler: emit forecast gating fields in decision log (bucketed confidence)
tests: add gating unit tests and 'no behavior change' guard
wiring: controller injects provider (default null) and config defaults
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Please confirm this cannot accidentally scale above current reactive desired if someone flips a config without the provider in place. I don’t want a partially-wired state to affect actuation.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep — even with predictive_scaling.enabled=true the stub provider always returns status=unavailable so gate_reason=unavailable and we keep reactive desired. I added a test that asserts desired_replicas equals reactive_desired across all pools when provider is null/unavailable.
Karthik Iyer (review): Confidence bucketing is good. Can we also treat “confidence missing” as unavailable/low_confidence explicitly? I want the semantics to be crisp for the service implementation.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Done. If status=ok but confidence is undefined we set gate_reason=unavailable (and emit forecast_status=ok, confidence_bucket=unknown). Added unit coverage.
Logan Wright (review): Please be careful about decision log payload growth. Are these fields going to all events? Also, make sure we’re not emitting raw floats in metrics.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Only added to the structured decision event (already sampled) and confidence is emitted as a bucket string. No new high-cardinality metric labels in this PR.
Jordan Lee (review): Naming: “min_confidence” should live under predictive_scaling.* and we should default it via policy evaluation later. For now keep config local but match the schema we agreed on.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated names to predictive_scaling.min_confidence and added a TODO pointing to the policy-evaluated config wiring (ENG-2842 follow-up).
Mina Haddad (review): Minor: make sure region is passed through the interface; forecast will be region-aware for multi-region pools.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added region to the request struct and threaded it through call sites (even though null provider ignores it).
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Approved after no-behavior-change test landed.
Logan Wright (approval): Looks good; thanks for the bucketed confidence.
release_notes: Internal: autoscaler can ingest forecast signals via a new interface and emit confidence-gating annotations in decision logs (no behavior change by default).
